about: The work machine's tillr backend policy for spending the owner's Claude subscription first, with Amazon Bedrock as the fall-back. A drain names this file with --policy when it should run on the subscription; backend-policy.bedrock.json beside it is the same machine's Bedrock-only policy, and backend-policy.json is the personal machines' policy. Every seat first runs on the Claude Code command line (the claude adapter), and each seat names its own fall-back: the design seat falls back to pi-designer and the build, review and scout seats fall back to pi, both of which run on Bedrock through the pi adapter. A run the subscription refuses writes no report, so the drain fails it over to the seat's next backend in the same pass. Why and how: docs/design/tillr-claude-backend.md. Several policy files is the stopgap docs/design/tillr-convergence.md OQ-TC2 records: the target is that tillr names only seats and the machine's profile resolves them, at which point this file is deleted.
